newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds end higher, some predict declines.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds end higher, some predict declines.

text.p: Argentine bonds finished higher again Friday, as some players predicted that this session - the fourth consecutive one with gains - will likely be followed by profit-taking.
"The ghost of a rise in U.S. rates continues to float around and that will determine the market's development," said a trader.
Argentina's FRB Brady bond due 2005 rose 3/8 to 91-1/8, while the dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional rose $0.10 to 126.10.
And U.S. rate concerns are likely to return to the center stage again next week with the release of some key U.S. economic indicators including jobless figures.

Another trader said after this week's news of upgrades to several Argentine companies' credit ratings by Standard & Poor's the market picked up a good deal of confidence -- something which could make it slightly resilient to any downturn in U.S. markets.
In the money markets, call money rates were flat at 5.13 percent.
